FPR evidence notebook: the 17 counted items¶

Team M001, Real-Time Edge Digital Twin for Bearing Fault Diagnosis and RUL Prediction in OH-2 Centrifugal Pumps. ICS owner of the models: Muhammad Jaddoua. Final Prototype Review (FPR), 16 Nov 2026. Same structure as UP2_Evidence: summary, scorecard table, then one section per spec with its highest-level evidence.

Every status is computed in a cell from stored reports (found by glob, latest wins) and live runs, against the spec thresholds; nothing is typed in as MET. A missing report shows PENDING, a failed cell shows a grey badge instead of crashing. Specs owned by ME/COE outside the integrated set are MET on the owners' statement (2026-11-15); their artifacts are held by the owners and are not in this repo.

Data tags. [SIMULATION; endpoints resampled from rig windows, 1 bearing/fault, curve shape assumed] (ICS/integrated models: S7, IS2, IS3 data), [MEASURED on rig] (real rig windows, 14-15 Nov), [MEASURED host] (this PC), [CALCULATED], [CITED], [OWNER-SUPPLIED].

Limits, one line. No real run-to-failure data exists for 4 of 5 fault classes. Anchors are 5 physical bearings (healthy + one per fault). Test units are held-out simulated trajectories, not held-out bearings; the damage-curve shape is assumed. Rank 9 for S7/IS2/IS3 is not reachable with this data: the live demo is Rank 9 for the pipeline only.

How to run

cd AI-engine/notebooks; ../.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute FPR_Evidence.ipynb --inplace --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=-1 then ... --to html FPR_Evidence.ipynb. Re-run after v6_node_<utc>.json or fpr_is2_v6_node_*.json land: those cells pick them up automatically. The .NET 10 SDK on PATH is needed for the C5 and S9-rate live cells (otherwise they fall back to stored numbers and say so). Live demo: docker compose --profile fpr-demo up --build backend-fpr fpr-replay (or ./scripts/run-fpr-demo.ps1).

import time, json, platform, os, sys, warnings
T_START = time.time(); warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown, HTML, Image, update_display
import ppr_helpers as P
import up2_helpers as U
import fpr_helpers as F
P.seed_everything(P.SEED); F.style()
pd.set_option("display.width", 220, "display.max_colwidth", 140, "display.max_rows", 100)

def show(fig, name):
    p = F.save(fig, name); plt.show(); return p
def chart(fn, name, *a, **k):
    try:
        fig = fn(*a, **k)
        if fig is None: return None
        return show(fig, name)
    except Exception as e:
        plt.close("all"); display(U.missing(f"chart {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"))

What was done. The node-feature AI (v5_node, then v6_node) was trained and scored on simulated degradation trajectories whose healthy/fault endpoints are resampled from real rig windows; a feature-only physics twin was added; both run live in the real stack (replay -> receiver -> NodeEngine -> backend -> dashboard), which is the Rank 9 demo of the PIPELINE.

Honest limits, in one line. No real run-to-failure data exists for 4 of 5 fault classes. Anchors = 5 physical bearings (healthy + one per fault); test units are held-out simulated trajectories, not held-out bearings; the damage-curve family is assumed.

1. Scorecard (17 counted items, live)¶

C3 (node BOM cost) was excluded by the reviewer; 17 items are counted, the rubric bar is more than 75 % = 13. Two evidence columns: Demonstrated live = what ran in this notebook; Spec evidence rank = the course ladder (0-9) the spec's own data supports (honest ceiling, see the limits section). Tier tells whether the MET comes from artifacts computed here or from an owner's statement.

7. S7: RUL MAPE <= 15 % on the held-out degradation window¶

Definition (pre-registered): MAPE in hours over [detected onset, T_fail - 10 % of the span], averaged over faulted bearings of held-out simulated trajectories (rig_anchor test units), scored once (frozen choices file written before scoring). Evidence rank: 6 (simulation + data, stored report with seed, commit and command). The pipeline producing the RUL runs live (Rank 9, section 5/11), but the score depends on an assumed damage curve (labels are a monotone function of it), so Rank 6 is the ceiling. The trivial baseline (log-linear on one health index) and a wrong-shape control are reported beside it: if the baseline matched the model, the number would measure the assumed curve.

In [9]:

             source=f"{NH['contract']}_{(NH['utc'] or '')[:10]} report, cmd `{NH['command']}`, commit {NH['commit']}",
             step="needs real run-to-failure data (>= 3 bearings/fault) for a rank above 6", note=d7.get("note"))

8. S9: dashboard refresh >= 10 Hz with physics RUL + AI RUL + fault ID updated together¶

Two live parts: (a) the rate at a SignalR client against the real backend fed by the real receiver/replay path (scripts/fpr_replay.py, node-live source); (b) the fields: the share of faulted windows (stage >= 2) in which AI RUL, physics RUL, Miner D, class and stage are all present (section 5). On the live rig node the AI/physics RUL stay n/a (the node sends window features only and the rig has no run-to-failure trajectory): the fields exist only on the replay of simulated trajectories, which is why the tag is [SIMULATION]. Evidence rank: 9 for the pipeline (rate and fields run live); the RUL values inside are simulation-based.

Legs: host (live above: NodeEngine.predict p95, plus the stored receive -> backend ack p95 from the rig-day run) and the Wi-Fi node -> laptop hop, which is not measurable: the node sends no timestamp (firmware change needed). So the end-to-end spec is PARTIAL by construction: the status below is computed from whether every leg has a measurement. Evidence rank: 6 for the measured host legs (host data, no node timestamp); the full chain needs the timestamp.

10. IS2: physics-AI RUL agreement (wording v2) and IS3¶

IS2¶

Wording v2 (coach clarification): e = |RUL_phys - RUL_AI| / L_ref per window of the faulted bearing in true stages 1-3 after warm-up; MED <= T_MED and P95 <= T_P95 with thresholds frozen on validation (never on test) and all wrong-AI controls must FAIL on validation, otherwise the metric is too loose to mean anything. v1 literal (max <= 5 %) is reported beside it and fails. Honest limits: the twin and the AI read the same node features (common mode: agreement is consistency of two readings of one signal), simulated data, L_ref uses an assumed duty (P/C = 0.5). Evidence rank 6 at best (3 while pending).

13. Limits, and what would legitimately close the gaps¶

  • Data. No real run-to-failure data exists for 4 of 5 fault classes; the one real failure (ball BA-1) has an invalid rpm column. One physical bearing per fault, severities ESTIMATED on rig day. Test units are held-out simulated trajectories, not held-out bearings; the damage-curve family is assumed, so S7/IS3 labels are a monotone function of it. IS2 is common-mode (twin and AI read the same features) and its L_ref uses an assumed duty.
  • What this means for the ranks. S7, IS2, IS3: Rank 6 at most (simulation + data). The live replay demo is Rank 9 for the pipeline only. "Rank 9 for every spec" is not reachable with this data.
  • To close the gaps legitimately (needs data, not tuning): (1) >= 3 physical bearings per fault with measured severity, frozen in splits.json before fitting; (2) real run-to-failure runs with true RUL; (3) B2X genuinely wired (today B2X is a copy of B1Y, policy B2X := B2Y); (4) a node timestamp in the firmware so the Wi-Fi hop of IS1 can be measured; (5) a physics-twin input independent of the node features for IS2.
  • Not done on purpose. No synthetic "held-out bearings" built by jittering real windows; no re-tuning on test; no metric redefinition (v1 IS2 is reported beside v2).

What was done. The node-feature AI (v5_node, then v6_node) was trained and scored on simulated degradation trajectories whose healthy/fault endpoints are resampled from real rig windows; a feature-only physics twin was added; both run live in the real stack (replay -> receiver -> NodeEngine -> backend -> dashboard), which is the Rank 9 demo of the PIPELINE.

Honest limits, in one line. No real run-to-failure data exists for 4 of 5 fault classes. Anchors = 5 physical bearings (healthy + one per fault); test units are held-out simulated trajectories, not held-out bearings; the damage-curve family is assumed.
